:::{#rem-differential-entropy-vs-entropy}
#### Differential entropy differs from entropy

A [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) value is not a probability,
so the [surprisal of a continuous value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-surprisal-continuous)
and the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) of a continuous random variable
(the differential entropy)
behave differently from their discrete counterparts:

- **Sign.**
  A density can exceed $1$,
  so the surprisal $\surprisalf{x}$ and the differential entropy can be negative,
  as in the
  [uniform example](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#exm-entropy-uniform)
  [@cover2006elements, section 8.1].
  The entropy of a discrete random variable is never negative.
- **Units.**
  Rescaling changes the differential entropy:
  $\entropyf{aX} = \entropyf{X} + \log |a|$ for a constant $a \ne 0$ [@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.6.4].
  Measuring the same quantity in metres rather than centimetres therefore changes it.
  Adding a constant does not:
  $\entropyf{X + c} = \entropyf{X}$ [@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.6.3].
- **Not a limit of entropy.**
  Round a continuous $X$ to bins of width $\Delta$,
  which gives a discrete random variable $X^\Delta$.
  Then $\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta \to \entropyf{X}$ as $\Delta \to 0$ [@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.3.1].
  The entropy $\entropyf{X^\Delta}$ itself grows without bound as $\Delta \to 0$,
  so the differential entropy is not its limit.

:::
